deep.reconstruction:
Notation. Euler writes ∫(1/z^m)(1/y^n) for S(m,n) = Σ_{z≥1} z^{-m} Σ_{y≤z} y^{-n}. In the modern strict convention this is S(m,n) = ζ(m,n) + ζ(m+n), where ζ(m,n) = Σ_{z>y≥1} z^{-m} y^{-n}. He writes ∫1/z^k for ζ(k).

Two kinds of relation are in play.
- Method 1 (§§ before) gives the reflection identity S(m,n) + S(n,m) = ζ(m)ζ(n) + ζ(m+n). This is the stuffle relation.
- Method 2 expands ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n) by partial fractions into S-sums with binomial coefficients. Divergent ζ(1) terms are handled formally. This is a shuffle-type relation.

Weight 7 (end of §16).
- The case (6,1), from the previous page, gave S(6,1) = 4ζ7 − ζ2ζ5 − ζ3ζ4. Equivalently ζ(6,1) = 3ζ7 − ζ2ζ5 − ζ3ζ4, which is correct.
- The case (5,2) gives S(2,5) + 2S(3,4) + 3S(4,3) + 3S(5,2) = ζ2ζ5 + 6ζ3ζ4 + ζ7.
- Subtracting S(2,5)+S(5,2) = ζ2ζ5+ζ7 and 2[S(3,4)+S(4,3)] = 2ζ3ζ4+2ζ7 yields S(4,3) + 2S(5,2) = 4ζ4ζ3 − 2ζ7.
- The case (4,3): the S(6,1) and ζ6ζ1 terms cancel, leaving S(3,4) + 2S(4,3) + 2S(5,2) = 5ζ4ζ3 − ζ7. After reflection this is the same equation.
- Euler therefore concludes that only S(6,1) and the combination S(4,3)+2S(5,2) are determined. If either summand were known separately, S(3,4) and S(2,5) would follow by reflection.

Weight 8 (§17) begins with the case (7,1): ζ7ζ1 − ζ8 = S(7,1) − 2ζ2ζ6 − 2ζ4ζ4 − 2ζ6ζ2 + Σ_{k=1}^{7} S(k,8−k). This is used on the next page to isolate S(7,1).

Purpose. The section systematically evaluates double Euler sums of each weight m+n in terms of products of single zeta values. Weight 7 is the first odd weight where Euler's system fails to separate all the sums.
errors: No computational error on this page. The equations S(2,5)+2S(3,4)+3S(4,3)+3S(5,2)=ζ2ζ5+6ζ3ζ4+ζ7, S(4,3)+2S(5,2)=4ζ3ζ4−2ζ7 and S(3,4)+2S(4,3)+2S(5,2)=5ζ3ζ4−ζ7 all check numerically. With ζ(5,2)≈0.038573 and ζ(4,3)≈0.085165 the identities hold to 6 digits.

Conceptual gap: the conclusion 'nihil noui concludi possit' (nothing new can be concluded) is an artefact of the form of Euler's relations, not a genuine indeterminacy. In his (4,3) relation the ζ(6,1) contribution cancels, so it collapses to the (5,2) one. The genuine shuffle (Euler decomposition) relations are ζ2ζ5 = ζ(2,5)+2ζ(3,4)+3ζ(4,3)+5ζ(5,2)+10ζ(6,1) and ζ3ζ4 = ζ(3,4)+4ζ(4,3)+10ζ(5,2)+20ζ(6,1). Together with reflection and the known ζ(6,1) they are independent (the reduced system has determinant −2) and give ζ(5,2) = 5ζ2ζ5 + 2ζ3ζ4 − 11ζ7 and ζ(4,3) = 17ζ7 − 10ζ2ζ5. Euler's surviving relation is exactly the difference of the two genuine ones.
Printing typo in the original: 'er' for 'et' in 'm=4 er n=3'.

ideas.what: Evaluation S(6,1) = 4ζ(7) − ζ(2)ζ(5) − ζ(3)ζ(4), i.e. a case of the ζ(n−1,1) formula.
ideas.modern_name: Euler's formula for ζ(n−1,1) (double zeta of depth 2 with last index 1)
ideas.where_published: E477 and earlier correspondence; general formula stated in E477

ideas.what: Reflection S(m,n)+S(n,m)=ζ(m)ζ(n)+ζ(m+n) combined with partial-fraction product relations to reduce weight-7 double sums.
ideas.modern_name: Stuffle (harmonic product) plus shuffle/Euler decomposition formula: the double shuffle relations in depth 2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler for reflection; decomposition formula usually attributed to Euler; double shuffle framework to Zagier, Ihara–Kaneko–Zagier

ideas.what: Explicit statement that at weight 7 only ζ(6,1) and the combination ζ(4,3)+2ζ(5,2) are determined by his method.
ideas.modern_name: Partial evaluation of odd-weight double zeta values (full evaluation: odd-weight theorem)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Full odd-weight theorem: Euler (claimed/partial), proved by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn (1995) and Huard–Williams–Zhang (1996)

missed.claim: Euler leaves ζ(5,2) and ζ(4,3) separately undetermined. His own type of relations, if carried out without the cancellation that occurs in his (4,3) expansion, would have given ζ(5,2)=5ζ2ζ5+2ζ3ζ4−11ζ7 and ζ(4,3)=17ζ7−10ζ2ζ5. This thread was completed only in the 1990s.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical datum on the odd-weight theorem: in 1776 Euler's relations had rank 4, not 5, at weight 7. It is likely already noted by Borwein et al. and historians, so its novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine algebra within Euler's known double-sum programme. Its explicit admission of indeterminacy at weight 7, caused by a lossy form of the product relation, is interesting for the history of the odd-weight theorem. However, it is plausibly already known to specialists who have read E477.
transcription_corrections: 'm=4 er n=3' is a typo in the print itself ('et' intended); keep as is.
